title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Special Procedure Law for Maritime Litigation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Special Maritime Procedure Law

Fa Fa [2000] No. 7

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Special Maritime Procedure Law), having been deliberated and adopted at the 13th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress, was promulgated on December 25, 1999, and shall come into force on July 1, 2000. The Special Maritime Procedure Law is a special procedural system established to scientifically regulate maritime litigation procedures, protect the litigation rights of the parties, and correctly implement the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China and other substantive maritime laws. It is an important component of China's litigation legal system. In order to correctly implement and enforce the Special Maritime Procedure Law, effectively safeguard the rights of parties to engage in maritime litigation in accordance with the law, and uphold judicial fairness, we hereby notify the following:

1. People's courts at all levels, especially maritime courts and the high people's courts hearing appeals therefrom, shall fully understand the significance of implementing the Special Maritime Procedure Law, earnestly organize trial personnel to study and research this law article by article, strengthen training, accurately grasp the legislative intent, and diligently prepare for all aspects of its implementation and enforcement. At the same time, they shall further improve open trials, explain the law through case examples, and, in coordination with relevant departments, actively carry out publicity activities so that the general public and all sectors of society understand this law and enhance their legal awareness of conducting maritime litigation in accordance with the law.

2. Before July 1, 2000, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) and the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court shall apply to the trial of maritime and maritime-related cases. For cases accepted but not yet concluded during this period, litigation procedures already conducted in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law shall remain valid. From July 1, 2000, where the Special Maritime Procedure Law provides for a matter, it shall be strictly handled in accordance with the Special Maritime Procedure Law; where the Special Maritime Procedure Law does not provide for a matter, the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.

3. From July 1, 2000, except for maritime courts and their located high people's courts which accept maritime and maritime-related cases in accordance with the law, local people's courts at all levels shall strictly comply with the review and case-filing procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law and the Special Maritime Procedure Law, and shall not accept maritime and maritime-related cases in disguised form by altering the cause of action or adding third parties. Where the jurisdiction over a case between a maritime court and a local people's court is unclear, the matter shall be reported level by level to the superior people's court for instruction; if there is a dispute, it shall be handled in accordance with Article 10 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law.

4. From July 1, 2000, except for the enforcement of effective judgments, arbitral awards, and notarized creditor's documents with enforceable effect in accordance with the law, maritime courts and local people's courts at all levels shall not accept any application for property preservation to arrest a ship unless it is based on a maritime claim as stipulated in Article 21 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law.

5. From July 1, 2000, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Pre-litigation Arrest of Ships by Maritime Courts, the Provisions on Auction of Arrested Ships by Maritime Courts for Debt Settlement, and other judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court concerning maritime litigation procedures that conflict with the Special Maritime Procedure Law shall cease to be implemented.

6. People's courts at all levels shall continuously summarize experience in the process of implementing the Special Maritime Procedure Law. Any problems encountered during implementation shall be carefully studied, and opinions shall be submitted to this Court for instruction and report in a timely manner, so as to ensure the correct implementation and enforcement of the Special Maritime Procedure Law.

February 28, 2000
